title: Policy Orchestrator for Heterogeneous Deployment Strata
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a policy orchestration layer that compiles a single, human-readable deployment intent into environment-specific execution plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to enable parity in canary, A/B, and shadowing workflows while respecting environment constraints (network egress, tenant isolation, autoscaling primitives, KMS availability). This ticket focuses on the control-plane component (policy compiler + admission checks) and a lightweight agent contract for environment adapters.
acceptance_criteria: A policy compiler can take a single YAML/JSON rollout intent and emit 3 execution plans: hosted, dedicated, private
Admission checks run pre-rollout and surface a deterministic list of mismatch warnings that block deployment when constraints are unsatisfied
Shadow traffic adapter implemented for Private with no egress by supporting local mirror endpoints; Hosted/Dedicated use network mirror where available
Auto-rollback heuristics configurable per-environment and will trigger rollback when 3 consecutive SLO violations occur within a 10 minute window
Integration tests covering canary -> promote/rollback for each environment with synthetic traffic and mocked infra
Audit events emitted to the Console with per-stage metadata and links to execution plan artifacts
proposed_solution: Introduce 'Deployment Constraint Profiles' that enumerate capabilities and limits for each environment (max-batch-size, supports-traffic-mirroring, ksm-enabled, allowed-apis, max-concurrent-canaries)

Build a lightweight 'policy compiler' service that validates the user intent against a selected profile and produces an ordered plan of actions (create canary endpoint, attach shadow mirror, start metric probes, ramp percentages, promote)
Expose a policy schema (openapi-compatible) for rollout intents so PMs and Design can author reproducible experiments (A/B split, metric guards, weighted routing)
Implement an 'admission-check' phase in the control plane that runs before any infra changes; it returns a machine-readable report and a human summary for Console UI

Design a small adapter contract (gRPC/HTTP) so each environment implements environment-specific translators. The adapter is intentionally thin: it receives plan steps and translates to native primitives (Hosted: API routes + redis mirror; Dedicated: pool routing rules; Private: local sidecar + service mesh hooks)
Embed default rollback policies and allow overrides per rollout; provide telemetry hooks so the Optimize team can surface cost/latency tradeoffs post-rollout
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize constraint profile spec and default profiles for 'hosted', 'dedicated-small', 'dedicated-large', 'private-standard'
Week 2: Implement policy compiler prototype with 3 example intents and unit tests
Week 3: Build admission-check API and simple Console integration to display validation reports
Week 4: Implement adapters for Hosted and Dedicated (Private adapter skeleton delivered to on-prem team)
Week 5: Run cross-environment integration tests (synthetic traffic harness) and refine auto-rollback heuristics
Week 6: Pilot with internal Canary on a non-critical model and collect telemetry
Post-pilot: iterate on UX and expand to customer facing rollout if metrics stable
test_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler mapping rules and constraint validation
Integration tests: simulate canary, shadow, AB flows across 3 adapters using local test harness
Chaos test: simulate partial adapter failures (adapter timeout, permission denied) and verify safe-fail behaviors
SLO regression tests: synthetic traffic that triggers latency/cost/accuracy gates to exercise auto-rollback
Security review: ensure adapters do not leak secrets and audit events include sufficient context
risks_mitigation: Risk: Divergent semantics between adapters cause unintended rollout differences. Mitigation: strict conformance tests and a canonical test corpus of rollout intents
Risk: Auto-rollback noise (false positives) during bursty traffic. Mitigation: rolling window heuristics + metric smoothing + manual override
Risk: Private environments lack required primitives (no mirror, limited KMS). Mitigation: fallback implementations (local mirror, ephemeral keys) documented in profiles
Risk: Increased attack surface with adapters. Mitigation: mTLS for adapter comms, least-privilege roles, and security review before Private GA
